transcript:
Meeting header: Date/Time: 2026-12-07 15:00 PST; Duration: ~68 minutes; Attendees: Samir, Riley, Maya (Redwood) / Lena, Daniel, Priya, Alexei (Orbit Haven)

Summary: quick alignment on listing checklist + observability playbook, some back-and-forth about KMS and onprem / VPC constraints. Aim to run a 24h soak with staging traffic and validate canary with fallback routing.

[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Lena (Orbit Haven): Hi, Lena here. Daniel's on as well.
[00:08] Daniel (Orbit Haven): Morning, yeah, Daniel.
[00:10] Samir: Great. Riley, Maya from our side?
[00:12] Riley (Redwood SE): Riley here. I'll be driving the bench/telemetry stuff.
[00:15] Maya (Redwood CSM): Maya, I'll coordinate the timeline and follow ups.
[00:18] Priya (Orbit Haven): Priya — product. Alexei in security will chime in for KMS.
[00:22] Alexei (Orbit Haven): hi.

[00:25] Samir: Alright, goal for today: confirm what we need to show in the marketplace listing preflight, align on observability — i.e., which metrics you need to surface in your dashboards — and agree a canary and soak plan for the on-prem/VPC variant. If we can close on those, we can proceed to the sandbox run.

[00:40] Lena: Sounds good. Primary ask: we need P95 under 220ms for our customer-facing chat flows, and P99 under 500ms. Also uptime SLO of 99.9 for the dedicated offering. Can you map those to Redwood's metric model?
[00:58] Riley: yes, we can. We collect per-request timing, queuing time, kernel exec time and token emission time. We'll map P95/P99 to the end-to-end request including queuing. A quick note — if you plan long sequences we might need to switch kernel paths, that's when quantization and batch sizing affect P99.
[01:20] Daniel: On sequences — our median seq length is 48 tokens, with a 95th at 320 for some doc gen flows. We also have a lot of short chats, so mixed distribution. Is that a problem?
[01:34] Riley: mixture is fine but it means batching heuristics will change. For mixed workloads we often recommend dynamic continuous batching with small max batch size to keep latency true. We'll show a sample config. Also KV cache hits will greatly reduce per-token time for longer sessions.

[02:05] Priya: KMS — we need to know if Redwood supports customer-managed keys for both hosted and private deployment. Our compliance team insists on HSM-backed keys.
[02:19] Alexei: And audit log fidelity — we need per-request traces that show which key was used, who triggered it, and retention for 365 days.
[02:30] Riley: For Private (VPC/on-prem) we can plug into your KMS via KM S integrations — apologies, the auto transcript sometimes says KM S — but yes, we support customer KMS and HSMs in the private plane. We also emit structured audit logs; retention policy depends on your retention tier but we can stream logs to your SIEM.
[02:52] Alexei: Good. Need to validate the exact log schema. Can you share a sample?
[02:58] Riley: yes — I'll drop a sample cloudwatch/elasticsearch and syslog example. link: https://drive.redwood/example-audit-schema (note: placeholder link).

[03:20] Samir: Back to listing: the preflight has a few network gating items — egress IP ranges, private endpoint support, and helm operator permissions for onprem deployments. Do you have constraints?
[03:35] Daniel: Egress must be whitelisted, we have a narrow firewall policy, and we need static egress ranges for the canary. Also for the onprem adapter we need it to run as non-root and have pod security policies honored.
[03:51] Riley: We can provide a set of static IPs for the dedicated pods and a helm values file. The operator can be configured to run as non-root; we'll include the PSP bits. We'll also provide a preflight conformance script you can run in your cluster.

[04:12] Lena: Telemetry — what will we see in the Redwood console? We want per-route latency, token burn, cost per 1k tokens, and error classification (model timeouts, truncated outputs, 5xx).
[04:28] Maya: Console will show per-model and per-route double breakdowns. We'll surface token-level cost and a breakdown by kernel/queuing. For errors we have an error taxonomy and we can send you a CSV export or hook into webhooks for real-time alerts.
[04:50] Priya: Can we hook into our Sentry for traces?
[04:54] Riley: yes, we emit trace ids in the request headers that you can correlate. We'll include a sample integration doc.

[05:10] Daniel: For the soak, we want to inject our staging traffic for 24 hours across the dedicated variant and see telemetry. We also want to exercise failover to the hosted API in case of overload. How does Redwood handle fallback routing?
[05:25] Samir: We support policy-based routing. For the canary we can set a rule: primary route to dedicated pool; on threshold breach (CPU or latency) automatically fallback to hosted variant with a compatible model. We can also set shadowing for a no-impact test.
[05:44] Riley: Important note: model variants might differ (quantized vs full float) and that can change output characteristics. We'll include a changelog and a delta-eval if you want to do quality gating.

[06:15] Lena: Quality gating — yes, we need to ensure fallback doesn't change derp — sorry, I meant "derivation" of answers. We need config for automatic rollback if quality drops.
[06:25] Riley: We have eval hooks tied to prompt sets. You can define prompt-based monitors and set thresholds; if quality drops beyond the threshold we'll automatically failover or throttle.

[06:45] Alexei: Security: During canary we need to ensure tokens are ephemeral and theft risks are mitigated. Also SSO for the console access is needed for our SOC audit.
[06:58] Maya: We support SSO/SAML, RBAC per team, and token scoping for the API keys. We'll coordinate an SSO test.

[07:15] Daniel: On the telemetry side, give us the names of the metrics we'll need to ingest: request.latency.ms, kernel.exec.ms, queue.time.ms, tokens.emitted.count, kvcache.hit.rate, model.fallback.count, routing.fallback.count, error.5xx.count, etc.
[07:35] Riley: yes, and we'll provide a mapping doc. Also a sample Grafana dashboard JSON if you want to import. link: https://drive.redwood/sample-grafana.json

[08:02] Priya: We have a question on billing/meters: Marketplace listing will need metering data exported monthly and an invoiceable CSV to match our internal chargeback. Can you provide export of per-customer token usage and model version used?
[08:18] Samir: We provide per-tenant usage exports and can tag by model version. We'll surface a per-route per-model usage CSV and also an invoice API if you want programmatic pulls.

[08:40] Lena: Great. A couple of blockers we want to log: 1) Need sample logs/schema for compliance review. 2) KMS HSM vendor compatibility confirmed. 3) Static egress IPs and helm non-root configuration.
[08:57] Samir: Got it. We'll own 1 and 3; Alexei/Orbit will validate 2 with their vendor.

[09:10] Riley: To make the soak meaningful, can you share a 48h sample of real traces — just sequence lengths, inter-arrival times, and session affinity? That will let us configure batching and bench.
[09:22] Daniel: We'll share an anonymized trace. Expected size ~200MB gz.

[09:35] Samir: timeline proposal: share checklist + sample logs (Samir) by 12/10; sample trace from Orbit by 12/13; staging token and bench by 12/12 from Riley; soak run week of 12/15; follow-up canary planning week of 12/20. Does that align?
[09:52] Priya: yes align.

[10:00] Alexei: one more — audit retention 365 days is non-negotiable for us, and we need retention proof for the SOC review. How flexible is Redwood's retention tiers?
[10:12] Maya: We have retention tiers; for private deployments we can set 365d retention and export to your S3 bucket or SIEM. We'll include an export playbook.

[10:30] Riley: small gotcha: if you enable full request/response logging for 365d, that has cost and PII implications — we'll recommend sanitized logs plus trace ids. We'll add a redaction playbook.

[10:50] Lena: ok that's fine.

[11:05] Samir: Any outstanding questions before we wrap?
[11:10] Priya: Can you confirm the operator version that supports non-root and PSP?
[11:15] Riley: v1.14.2 and up. We'll send helm values file.

[11:30] Daniel: For the canary, we also want the ability to do traffic split 10/90 then 30/70 and monitor P95 — can Redwood do gradual ramping?
[11:40] Samir: yes, the rollout policy supports staged percentages with metrics gating between steps.

[11:55] Maya: Ok I'll summarize actions and owners and put it in the shared drive. We'll include links to the sample logs, helm values, and bench scripts.

[12:10] Samir: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the checklist and sample artifacts.
[12:17] Lena: thanks all.
[12:20] call ended

Notes: transcription has minor mis-hears (KM S -> KMS, some proper nouns), purposeful informal speech and crosstalk in places. Artifacts referenced: drive link to preflight checklist and sample telemetry/grafana JSON.
